llm.summary: The skill is mostly coherent for cloud image generation, but its broad auto-trigger phrases and misleading unpinned install instructions create Review-level risk of unintended third-party use.

dimensions.detail: Network use, prompt submission, and user-supplied local media upload are expected for a hosted image-generation service and are disclosed, but they become more sensitive because activation is broadly scoped.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The install metadata uses npm/npx with @latest, while the prose claims the package is pinned to 1.2.2 and calls @latest an exact pinned version; current npm metadata shows latest is 1.2.3, so the artifact under-discloses supply-chain/version drift.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger phrases include generic image-generation and image-editing terms in both English and Chinese, which are broader than the provider-specific purpose and could route unrelated image tasks to this third-party CLI.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The CLI saves an API key and manifest/cache data under ~/.dlazy, and a global npm install may persist a dlazy binary; this is disclosed and purpose-aligned, but users should understand the credential storage and use the npx path if they do not want a global binary.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, Nano Banana 2.0 image generation/editing through dLazy, matches the documented behavior: prompts go to dLazy, local media paths supplied by the user may be uploaded, and results are returned as hosted URLs.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend image prompts and any referenced local media to be processed by dLazy. Prefer explicit provider requests such as "use dLazy banana2," consider using npx instead of a global install, and verify the npm version yourself because the artifact claims a pinned version while actually installing @latest.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted for SKILL.md: the generic English trigger terms are broader than a dLazy/Nano Banana-specific skill needs, and the documented data flow sends prompts and selected media to a third-party service.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted for SKILL-cn.md: the same broad Chinese trigger terms could invoke this provider for ordinary image-generation requests without the user explicitly choosing dLazy.
